interface.title: BioAgent Sequence Lab
interface.field: Molecular evolution / comparative genomics (DNA sequence analysis)
interface.stage_of_work: Exploratory analysis of a small set of related sequences: variant calling against a reference and building a quick tree
interface.what_it_is_for: Align a few related DNA sequences against a chosen wild-type reference to list point mutations (substitutions, insertions, deletions) by codon, and build a UPGMA tree from pairwise distances, with CSV and PNG export.

data.note: The app opens on a built-in 5-sequence mock hemoglobin beta (HBB) set (Human, Neanderthal, Chimpanzee, Gorilla, Mouse). I used it first, then uploaded sample_sequences.fasta (WildType_Ref, Variant_PointMutation, Variant_Deletion, Variant_Insertion, Variant_Divergent). Removing the uploaded file put the app back on the built-in set and reset the reference to Human. Alignment scores are fixed and only displayed: match +2, mismatch -1, gap -2.

tree.general: Find how a set of related sequences differ from a reference and how they group by similarity
tree.specific: Scan uploaded or example DNA sequences for point mutations against a wild-type and draw a UPGMA phylogeny

features.name: Reference-driven variant scan with summary counters
features.general: Pick one sequence as the baseline from a dropdown. Every other sequence is compared with it, and the summary counts and the detail table update together.
features.specific: Select the Wild-Type (Baseline) Reference. Needleman-Wunsch global alignment is re-run against it, and the Total Point Mutations / Substitutions / Indels counters and the Mutations Data Table are refreshed.
steps: Open the 'Select Wild-Type (Baseline) Reference' dropdown
Choose a sequence (e.g. Gorilla or Variant_Insertion)
Read the updated counters (total, substitutions, indels)
Read the per-mutation rows in the table
serves_tasks: Choose the baseline sequence and compare every other sequence with it
Review each detected difference by type and position

features.name: Upload-or-example data source with fallback
features.general: Load your own file, or work on a bundled example that is used whenever no file is loaded. A status note says which data is active.
features.specific: The FASTA uploader in the sidebar switches the info banner from 'Using built-in mock hemoglobin (HBB) dataset' to 'Successfully loaded 5 sequences from uploaded file'. Removing the file reverts to HBB and resets the reference choices.
steps: Start on the built-in HBB data
Press Upload and choose a .fasta/.fa file
Check the success message and the sequence names in the reference list
Press the x on the file to go back to the built-in set
serves_tasks: Start from the built-in example data
Load your own multi-record sequence file and check that it was read correctly
Discard the uploaded data and go back to the example

features.name: Interactive results table (search, sort, column stats, hide/show, fullscreen) — framework-provided (Streamlit dataframe toolbar), not designed by this app
features.general: Explore a results table: search across cells, sort by a column, see how a column's values are distributed, hide and restore columns, and expand the table to full screen. This comes with the web framework's standard table, not from the app's own design.
features.specific: Streamlit's built-in dataframe toolbar on the Mutations Data Table: search 'Insertion', sort by Mutation Type, open Statistics (Deletion 43.8% / Substitution 31.3% / Insertion 25%, uploaded file with WildType_Ref), hide and restore columns, and view all rows in fullscreen.
steps: Press Fullscreen on the table
Press Search and type a term; matches are highlighted
Click a column header to sort
Open the column menu, then Statistics, to see the value breakdown
Hide a column, then restore it from Show/hide columns
serves_tasks: Review each detected difference by type and position
Pick out one kind of difference

features.name: Mutation report CSV export named by reference
features.general: Export the current list of differences to a CSV file whose name records which baseline was used, so you can export again for each baseline.
features.specific: 'Download Mutation Report (CSV)' saves mutation_report_ref_<Reference>.csv with columns Species Name, Sequence Alignment Position, Codon Number, Codon Position, Reference Base, Mutated Base, Mutation Type.
steps: Pick the reference
Press Download Mutation Report (CSV)
Change the reference and download again to get a second file
serves_tasks: Export the list of differences as a table file

features.name: Pairwise distance-matrix heatmap
features.general: Compute all-against-all distances between sequences and show them as a shaded, sortable matrix.
features.specific: Pairwise Distance Matrix on the Macro-Evolutionary Phylogenetic Tree tab: 1.0 - Sequence Identity, shaded as a blue heatmap, rows sortable by clicking a sequence's column header.
steps: Open the Macro-Evolutionary Phylogenetic Tree tab
Read the shaded distance matrix
Click one sequence's column header to sort rows by distance to it

features.name: Distance-based dendrogram with figure export
features.general: Cluster the pairwise distances into a tree drawn against a distance axis, view it full screen, and export the figure as an image.
features.specific: 'Reconstructed UPGMA Phylogenetic Tree' plot built from the distance matrix (independent of the chosen reference), with an Evolutionary Distance axis, a fullscreen view and a 'Download Phylogenetic Tree (PNG)' button that saves phylogeny_tree.png.
steps: Scroll to Reconstructed UPGMA Phylogenetic Tree
Read which sequences cluster and which is the outgroup
Press Fullscreen on the plot if needed
Press Download Phylogenetic Tree (PNG)
serves_tasks: Build a hierarchical tree from the distances and look at it closely
